chapter: Childhood and first bands in Ohio
title: Speed Webb's band and its star personnel
summary: Jackson lists Speed Webb's trumpets, trombones, saxophones and rhythm section, including Teddy Wilson, Roy Eldridge and Vic Dickinson, and says he has never played with a sad band.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Who's this? Speed Webb?
Yeah. But the band, the guys he had in that band -- Teddy Wilson was with that band at the time.
Yeah, Teddy. Who else was in? Anybody else you remember?
Sure. The trumpet section was Reynauld Jones and Steve Dunn from Cincinnati and Roy Eldridge.
Wow.
And the trombones was Gus Wilson, which was Teddy's brother, and Vic Dickinson.
That's Teddy Wilson's brother?
Dickenson
Yeah, and Vic Dickinson.
Wow.

And the saxophones was Leonard Gaye, Smoke Richardson, and Chuck -- I forget Chuck's last name. He was from Detroit. And of course Teddy on the piano and Bowles was on bass. I think Bowles later went to Chicago to live.
Uh-huh.
And the drummer's name and guitar name I can't remember either. But they were very good. The drummer used to drum like the old Walter Johnson style, very smooth.
But they had a lot of good arrangements because Gus was writing then, you know. Gus was a very good arranger.
That's Teddy's brother Gus?
Yes, a very good arranger. And, gee whiz, they had -- the soloists they had, oh, wow. But --
Those are still great names, all those powerful names.
Are they, are they?
Yes, yes, indeed.
But, you know, Milt, I've been lucky. I've never played with what I could call, what you call a real sad band. I've never played with a sad band in my life. I've been that lucky.
